about: How AI clones a voice from 3 seconds. Factory #18, backlog row 19, playlist How AI works. One hard idea: to a voice-cloning model, your voice is just numbers. Checkable by every viewer: Microsoft's VALL-E paper (arXiv 2301.02111, submitted Jan 5, 2023) and its research page (read 2026-11-01): 'synthesize high-quality personalized speech with only a 3-second enrolled recording of an unseen speaker as an acoustic prompt'; 'This page is for research demonstration purposes only.' Mechanism from the paper: a neural audio codec (EnCodec) turns sound into discrete codes ('given a 10-second waveform, the discrete representation is a matrix with 750 x 8 entries', so 3 s = 225 x 8 = 1,800 codes, our math), the language model predicts new codes 'conditioned on a phoneme sequence x and an acoustic prompt matrix', and the codec decoder turns them back into sound. Condition from the page: 'the similarity, and naturalness depend on the length and quality of the speech prompt'. Stake, dated: FBI PSA I-120324-PSA, Dec 3, 2024: 'Criminals generate short audio clips containing a loved one's voice to impersonate a close relative in a crisis situation, asking for immediate financial assistance or demanding a ransom.' Tip, same page: 'Create a secret word or phrase with your family to verify their identity.' Hero: the paper voice tape (8 rows of number tiles) with the coral stamp JUST NUMBERS in the 1.2 s silence after 'just numbers.'; screenshot hold = whole tape frame, >= 1.2 s still. No how-to beyond the paper's high-level pipeline. Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times. Two planned silences for sound: 1.2 s after 'numbers.' (hero thump) and 0.9 s after 'voices.' (FBI folder slap).

So how does AI voice cloning work?

lines.say: It's in Microsoft's own twenty twenty-three paper.

lines.text: First, those three seconds become 1,800 numbers.
lines.say: First, those three seconds become eighteen hundred numbers.

lines.text: Then it predicts numbers for words you never said.
